Definition: to strip off, i.e. (partially) scrape; by implication, to segregate (as an angle)
BiblicalUsage: To strip off is the word for scraping a house and measuring a court: he shall cause the house to be scraped within round about, and they shall pour out the dust without the city into an unclean place, and in the four corners of the court there were courts joined.
TheologicalSignificance: I read the scraping as the cleansing of the house, and the measuring as the order of the temple.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
